events.body:
Rain has dissolved the pharmacy sign until only the green cross is left of it, and the runoff from the awning has cut a clean channel through the dust in the doorway.

Three people come out through the broken window in a spread they have obviously practiced. The woman takes the left with a hunting bow already strung, and she is looking for somewhere to rest the limb; the window ledge is the nearest thing. The man behind her limps, and he does not come forward at all. He stands in the mouth of the alley, which tells you where the way out is. The boy is the third. He holds his knife at the wrong angle and keeps checking the woman for what to do with his face.

Empty cure cartons blow around your boots, printed with the names of illnesses nobody can treat now. All three are watching your pack. None of them has looked at your face.

outcomes.victory:
You are inside the arrow’s arc before the bow limb reaches the ledge. The shot goes into the shopfront behind you, and after that it is close work, and short.

The limping man does not try. He takes the boy by the collar and hauls him into the alley, and the boy keeps his head turned the whole way, so whatever account of this reaches anyone will be in his words. Their canned meat is stamped for a hospital ward. You pack it beside the shaped metal they had been filing into arrowheads, still bright along the cut edges. A chain wrench hangs among their tools, and you take it.
outcomes.critical_victory:
You catch the limb on its way up and turn it across her, and the pistol is out of her belt and into your hand before she has finished deciding which weapon this is. She lets go of both and steps back under the green cross with her palms open, like she practiced.

The other two go down the alley without waiting for her. Four cartridges sit in the pipe frame beside a string of filed dog teeth, and the pharmacy dust on the grip holds a whole print of the hand that carried it. She is alive behind you when you leave, and she watches you take both.

outcomes.success:
You go straight at the limping man rather than around him, on the side he cannot turn quickly, and you are past his reach before the bow comes up behind you. A warped service door takes your shoulder and gives.

The stockroom is dark and full of tipped shelving. You cross it on broken glass and out through the delivery bay, and you do not stop for two streets. Nobody died at the pharmacy. The gang keeps the corner and their account of a stranger who would not stay to argue, and the sprint stays in your legs for the rest of the afternoon.
outcomes.failure:
The alley narrows where a refrigerator went over on its side, and going over it puts your back to the window for as long as that takes. The arrow crosses your ribs on the way down the other side. It arrives as heat rather than pain; the pain waits until the laundry yard.

You get out. You get out slowly, with your shirt bunched against yourself and one hand holding it there, listening to them not follow, because they do not have to. Everything from here is going to cost more than it did this morning.

outcomes.success:
You cough into the crook of your sleeve and go on coughing, then name the symptoms off the old quarantine posters in the order the posters used them, the way somebody would who had read them while waiting in a corridor.

The boy goes first. He steps back into the man behind him, and the fear travels through the three of them faster than any argument could have. The bow comes down last. They open a gap wide enough for a plague and hold it there while you walk through, and not one of them puts out a hand to test whether you are lying.
outcomes.failure:
She lets you finish. Then she tells you your eyes are clear and your hands are steady, and asks the boy which of those a sick traveler gets to keep.

Nobody hits you. The limping man holds your pack open while she goes through it and takes her price for the time you wasted out of whatever is in there, and you stand still for it, because the bow has not moved once. All the way up the street behind you the boy is repeating your symptoms to the others as a joke, and getting the order right.

events.body: An evacuation bus rests across two lanes, its tires melted into shallow black pools. Someone wired the rear doors together from inside and pressed strips of family photographs into the rubber seal. Soot blinds every window except one circle rubbed clear at a child’s height. Through it you can count what is stacked under the driver’s seat: two flat ration wrappers and the shoulder of a sealed bottle. The doors will only open by force. Through the same circle, torn paneling has exposed the emergency release cable, and a first-aid bracket hangs beside it, clips still shut.

outcomes.success: The frame groans apart beneath steady pressure. Inside, seat belts bind empty blankets into the shapes of sleeping passengers. Two ration bars and a sealed bottle remain under the driver’s seat, overlooked when whoever wired the doors chose another exit.
outcomes.failure: The corroded frame releases all at once and hammers your shoulder against the step. Pain locks the joint before you can pull free. The doors remain crossed by wire, and every attempt to lift your arm confirms how badly the impact twisted it.

outcomes.success: You follow the release cable beneath torn wall panels until your fingers find its manual catch. The doors fold inward without disturbing the photographs. A first-aid pouch yields clean bandages, and the cable bracket supplies metal small enough to carry.
outcomes.failure: The emergency circuit still holds one poisonous breath. When your tool bridges the terminals, the battery case splits and vents sweet metallic vapor into your face. You stagger outside with watering eyes, a burned throat, and contamination prickling across exposed skin.

events.body: Six dogs hunt between abandoned cars without barking, scarred shoulders bare beneath trailing blue leashes. The largest tests your scent from a concrete divider while the rest spread wide. Their blanket nest blocks the eastern lane.

outcomes.victory: The pack breaks. You finish the largest on the divider and strip its nest: a brush machete and shaped metal worth carrying.

outcomes.outcome: You throw the can beneath the divider. Hunger collapses their discipline into snapping bodies, and you pass reading old names stamped on their collars.

outcomes.success: Your hands find the divider’s edge before the pack closes. You vault to the far lane and keep moving, beyond the reach of teeth.
outcomes.failure: Your boot turns on the divider and drops you badly. The barrier holds the dogs off while your ankle swells against every step after.

events.body:
Advertising tarps are strung from the supermarket’s fallen sign to the trolley bays, and everything under them takes their color: red at one end of the forecourt, yellow at the other. Twelve traders have laid out batteries, roots, boiled cloth, and things that are worth anything here only because somebody carried them this far.

Nobody calls a price aloud. A woman stitching a filter into a gas mask keeps her eyes on the seam and her attention on the road you came in by, because part of the rate is what you know. Two tables along, a boy weighs scrap on a kitchen scale. Behind him a salvage table of cracked dolls and plastic tools carries one indicator light, pulsing at an interval too even for a fault.

There is an unsplit woodpile behind her stall and a water queue behind his, and both of them look at you as though an afternoon of labor is also a currency.

outcomes.success:
You give her what the road behind you actually gave you: a collapsed lane, standing water in the gutter, and a delivery truck that blocks the next bend from view. She stops stitching in the middle of the third detail and makes you say the truck again.

Then she pays without haggling, in boiled bandages rolled tight and a strip of tablets still in their foil, which is better than anything she has offered this morning. All down the row, traders begin moving their best stock off the tables nearest the road you just described.
outcomes.failure:
You are the third traveler this week to arrive from the same side of the city, and she has already heard two versions of a road report nobody could check. She hears you out because it costs her nothing, then goes back to the seam.

A vendor further along either takes pity or takes the opportunity, and fills a bottle from the communal filter for whatever scrap your pockets can spare. You leave the row with water you can drink and an exact price on a story that did not buy much.

outcomes.success:
The pulse is too even to be a fault. You handle worse things first, a doll with a split face, a plastic wrench, and you set the scanner down twice before you buy it, so the price stays where it is.

Outside the tarps you turn it over and hold the screen flat to the concrete. It finds a seam, then the space under the seam, then the reinforcement running through both. The seller listened to it click for a season and filed it with the toys, and you are not going back in to explain that.
outcomes.failure:
The indicator is bright because a capacitor behind it is leaking, and you learn that with the casing already open across your knees. The board comes apart in flakes at the first touch, dry as stove ash.

By the time you look up, the seller has closed on another bargain two tables down and cannot pick you out of the afternoon’s strangers. Nobody at the tables says anything about it. Being wrong in public here is treated as a private matter, and that is the whole of the kindness available.

outcomes.outcome:
You split the mask-maker’s woodpile with the hatchet she keeps for it, and it takes what is left of the afternoon. The head sits loose on the handle, so you learn to swing around the wobble. She brings you water twice without being asked.

When the pile is stacked she puts the hatchet into your hands instead of coins: rust across the head, a handle worn into the shape of somebody else’s grip. Your scrap is still in your pocket, unsold, and the row has folded up around you while you worked.

The boy with the kitchen scale wants water hauled from the standpipe and his crates moved before the tarps come down, and he counts the trips out loud, which is how you learn he has done this arithmetic with adults before.

At dusk he pays out of the space behind his stall: a bat with roofing nails driven through the meat of it and the heads filed off flush. He had been keeping it for a night nobody wants to be ready for. You spent the whole evening with his stock in your arms and never once got to bargain over any of it.

events.body: The overpass ends mid-air above a rail cutting, two reinforcement bars bridging the gap with wind-polished faces. A school bus hangs nose-down from the far edge. A drainage channel curves east below, low and foul.

outcomes.success: You cross sideways, boots where concrete still grips steel. The bus shifts once and settles. Intact roadway receives you with daylight to spare.
outcomes.failure: A bar rolls under your sole and slams you against the broken edge. You haul up with a swollen ankle, torn palms, and the quick route paid in pain.

outcomes.success: The channel stays shallow, though oily water reaches your knees and the ceiling shoves your pack sideways. You emerge smelling of sewer, tired and hungrier.
outcomes.failure: A collapsed grate forces you crawling through a shoulder-wide pipe. Runoff soaks your wrappings while concrete fights every movement. Daylight returns late.

events.body:
A white curtain moves in and out of a third-floor window on a burned apartment block. Every other window on that face is open to the weather. This one still holds glass along its lower edge, which is what gives the curtain something to breathe against.

Fresh chalk on the entrance frame says NOT THE STAIRS, in a hand steady enough to have taken its time over the letters. The ground-floor hall smells of wet plaster, and the street behind you is still perfectly audible, which is the last comfortable thing about this building.

Above, a cupboard door taps twice, pauses, then taps again. You take one step toward the stairwell and the rhythm changes. On the first landing, drifted against the wall, lie dozens of shed plates the size of a spread hand, dry and slightly curved, stacked the way broken roofing slate stacks. Somebody has written SHUTTER SKITTERS beside them. The treads above are soft with damp, and the tapping starts again inside the wall at your shoulder.

outcomes.success:
The stair holds if you keep to the wall side and put your weight on the outer end of each tread. The curtain is tied to a cracked latch and pulls whenever air crosses the room; it has been doing that for months, and nobody has lived here since the fire.

The provisions are in a cupboard with towels packed around them, each one wrapped twice in oilcloth, against smoke or against something smaller than smoke. A sealed medicine kit. A can. You go down faster than you came up, and the tapping keeps pace with you inside the wall as far as the door.
outcomes.failure:
The tread you trust is the one that has been holding water. It gives at the center without any sound of warning and drops you onto the landing below, where your head finds the radiator on the way past.

You come around with plaster in your mouth and the light doing something wrong at its edges. Getting out means crawling, and choosing a direction to crawl in takes several attempts, because the street keeps arriving from a side it should not be on. The cupboard is still tapping when you reach the door, on a rhythm that has changed again.

outcomes.outcome:
You read the chalk a second time and decide it was written by somebody who knew this building better than an afternoon could teach you. The plates in the drift are dry, and there are a great many of them, and every part of the third floor is a guess made from the hall.

You leave the curtain to its patient work above the street. Whatever is wrapped in that cupboard stays wrapped, the warning stays on the frame for the next traveler, and the tapping goes on behind you for as long as the block is in earshot.

outcomes.victory:
You keep the light on the landing and drive the colony away from the stair in bursts, never letting it close into the armored sheet it wants to become. Plates skitter through the broken door and vanish into the colder hall below.

The cupboard is still there when the tapping stops. Its towels have done their work: a sealed medicine kit and a can are dry inside their oilcloth. You leave the chalk warning where it was. The street sounds close and ordinary again when you step out.

events.body:
The siren on the municipal garage roof begins to turn without anything having asked it to. What comes out is half a note, over and over, cut short each time the rotor swings away from you. Pigeons come off the roofs in sheets. The sound goes down the avenue and keeps going, out past blocks you cannot see into.

Down there, doors are opening. Not swinging in a draft: opening, one and then another, in still air, on a street where nothing else is moving.

The service ladder is bolted up the garage wall in full view of all of it, and it is intact. At its foot a stencil reads TOWER SIX, and a maintenance card gone gray behind cracked plastic names the motor cutoff and the panel it sits in. Whoever kept this machine alive wrote down how to stop it. Every unfinished cry tells the district that something out here has started moving again.

outcomes.success:
You climb between cries with your hands closed around the outside of the rails, because the ladder rings through every pass of the rotor. The cutoff is where the card says it is, fused half open. You pull it by hand.

The rotor keeps turning a while longer, slower, quieter, and then the whole district is holding still. The shapes on the avenue are three streets off with nothing left to walk toward. You come down carrying the charge pack and two useful lengths of wire, and the smell of scorched insulation stays on your hands for hours.
outcomes.failure:
Your tool bridges the housing while the rotor is still coming round, and the current goes up through both hands and lets go of you again on its own schedule. You keep hold of the ladder without having decided to. The siren goes on screaming a hand’s width above your head.

You get down. It takes a long time and you do not remember much of it afterward. Your palms have gone shiny across the pads, and for the rest of the day every quiet sound has that half note starting underneath it.

outcomes.success:
You decline to answer the machine’s panic with any of your own. You choose a pace you can hold and you hold it, east, past the garage and the dead traffic lights and out of the avenue.

Two blocks, then four. The tower goes on calling behind you, and the shapes coming into the district have a fixed thing to walk toward that is not you. The note thins and finally goes out. What is in your legs by then is the honest weight of distance, and the tower is still working, still telling anyone else out here where to look.
outcomes.failure:
You leave, and the sound comes with you around every corner, and each returning note reads as nearer than the one before it. You start checking alleys. You double back twice, on a loose gutter and on a dog.

By the time distance finally takes the siren, you have spent more of the afternoon on it than the ladder would have cost, and almost none of that ground was covered in a straight line. Long after there is nothing left to hear, your attention keeps swinging back on the same slow interval.

events.body: A yellow civil-defense locker crouches under the courthouse stairs behind fallen stone. Four-language instructions cover its door, soot-burned line by line. The lock looks both thief-proof and breakable. A road-sign buckler hangs on the hook beside it.

outcomes.success: The lock tears away with half its bracket. Two bottles and two ration bars wait behind evacuation forms, seals clean under courthouse dust.
outcomes.failure: The bracket splits hooked and opens your palm before the lock moves. Blood dots the instructions as you pull back. The cut keeps working open.

outcomes.success: Missing words survive across languages. You rebuild the sequence and turn the lock through three reluctant positions. Tablets and a folded bandage wait inside.
outcomes.failure: The final turn drives a bolt across the mechanism. One hard click turns the locker into a box without an entrance. You leave blind to its contents.

outcomes.outcome: You lift the buckler off its hook and leave the locker sealed. Hammered road sign, fitted strap, battered rim. Whatever waits behind the door stays unknown.

events.body:
A handheld radio hangs by its strap from a traffic-light cable at head height, and it is talking. A child’s voice, recorded, reads out a set of coordinates, then asks whether Talia can hear this, then runs out and starts again. It has been saying it long enough for the words to have worn smooth.

Between repetitions the channel does not go dead. It hisses, and under the hiss somebody is breathing with a handset open, near enough to the microphone that you can hear them swallow. They are listening to the loop as well.

The rooftops around you carry a district’s worth of aerials and sagging line, and the signal could be coming off any of four of them. Answering tells whoever is breathing that a stranger with a working set is standing on this corner. Finding them says nothing to anybody.

outcomes.success:
A woman comes onto the channel before you finish the second landmark. She gives you the water tower and waits for you to place it, and only when you place it correctly does she say Talia Vale. Behind her, two children are arguing over a blanket, close to the handset, unworried about being heard.

You hand her the tarp market in things she can confirm from where she stands. She reads it back in the wrong order on purpose and lets you correct her. The channel stays open longer than it needs to, then closes, and you go east hearing how your own voice sounds when somebody is listening.
outcomes.failure:
You give the directions clearly and completely, then give them again more slowly, in case the first pass was stepped on. Nothing acknowledges any of it. The recorded child asks whether Talia can hear this, runs out, and begins asking again.

The breathing under the hiss never changes once while you speak, which is when it occurs to you that it may not be a person, or may be a person who has decided what strangers are. You lower the handset with the loop still running, and for the rest of the afternoon you catch yourself listening to open air the same way.

outcomes.success:
You take readings under three separate runs of line and walk the differences until the needle stops arguing with itself. The transmitter is in a maintenance cabinet on the fourth roof: a relay kit wired to a car battery, with a directional antenna clamped to the parapet and aimed.

Nobody is there, and nobody has been for a while. The kit gives up its compass and a fistful of components, and the antenna is still pointing exactly where somebody set it, which is the corridor the message was cut to travel down. You have their bearing in your hand and you have never spoken to them.
outcomes.failure:
Concrete and hanging cable throw the signal back at you from every direction. Each bearing looks conclusive for as long as it takes to walk it, and then the strength climbs behind you instead of ahead.

You cross the same intersection three times before accepting that the corner itself is the problem and no amount of patience will solve it from here. The hour is gone and your concentration with it. The loop is still running when you come back to the cable, asking whether Talia can hear this, and it will go on asking whoever stands here next.

outcomes.outcome: You leave the handset where it hangs, its loop carrying on for whoever reaches this corner next. The child asks for Talia again as you move out of range. You do not know whether anyone beneath the hiss heard your footsteps, and you do not test it. The traffic light sways once on its cable, then settles. You have given no answer and learned no bearing.

events.body: The intersection has folded into utility tunnels, traffic lights still changing color over the hole. The eastern road crosses a two-stride lip of root-held asphalt. Below sits a maintenance shelf, its ladder ending mid-air. Coughing rises from underneath.

outcomes.success: You take the lip where roots hold the asphalt whole and cross in one committed step. Gravel spills behind you. The hour a slow climb would have cost stays yours.
outcomes.failure: The edge breaks at takeoff and throws you against the far wall. You catch a cable and climb out, ankle twisted, every step ahead demanding pain.

outcomes.success: The rope holds after the ladder bolts fail. On the shelf you recover clean water and compact tools from a sealed box. Nothing below learns more than your breathing.
outcomes.failure: The shelf pulls free at your touch. Your rope catches the fall and swings you into a pipe, scattering tools into black water. You climb back exhausted and empty-handed.

outcomes.victory: The last coughing dog drops on the concrete. Its nest holds a sealed poultice and workable scrap. Your pulse stays high and eager for the next two miles.

events.body:
The barricade is truck doors wired end to end across the only raised track above the salt, and the people behind it have had you in sight for an hour. Five collectors wear pieces of one transit uniform faded five different colors. The oldest sits under a striped umbrella with a revolver flat across his thighs and does not stand when you arrive, which is a statement he has clearly made before.

The clerk is younger than the rest and keeps a school exercise book braced on her forearm. She writes a line for every traveler: what they carried, which way they went, what they paid. Their toll maintains the road east, she says, reading it off the page.

Behind the barricade the wheel ruts run on into glare past marker posts nobody has straightened in years. On both flanks the pan lies open to the horizon with no wreck and no rise on it.

outcomes.victory:
The umbrella goes down first. After that the barricade is five people who never planned for anyone to walk straight at it, and they come apart along their own seams: the two youngest run north across open pan, the man in the chair drops the revolver rather than reload it, and the rest follow whoever moved first.

You take the dropped revolver and three heavy cartridges from the tin beside the chair, a bracket cut for salvage, and one can of their evening meat. A brass precinct star rides in the chair's crease, pinned where only its wearer knew. The exercise book stays open at your page.

outcomes.success:
You ask the clerk which stretch of road her book says the toll repaired. She turns two pages looking for it while the others watch her do it, and the silence that follows is the whole of the negotiation. The man under the umbrella tells her to settle it and be finished.

She prices you at one ration and takes what your pack will give up toward it, entering the figure in a careful hand. Then she keeps her voice under the wind. The crater route killed two collectors yesterday, she says. Both of them are written in this book, and nobody has crossed the lines out yet.
outcomes.failure:
They hear a negotiation as proof that you can afford to stand here and have one. Two of them work your pack while the clerk holds the page flat against the wind, and every item lifted out is announced as a separate fee: inspection, weighing, the trouble of writing you down.

They stop when the pack stops yielding, sooner than they expected, which does nothing for their mood. The barrier goes up. Behind you the clerk finishes her line, and you understand within ten steps that the book, not the road, is what the toll is actually for.

outcomes.success:
You go wide, far enough into the glare that the barricade shrinks to a dark pin and the umbrella stops being a color. There is no cover out here and no need for any. At that distance on open salt a walking person is indistinguishable from rising heat.

The loop costs most of the afternoon and a bad hour finding the track again through haze that erases the difference between ground and sky. Nobody opens your pack. Nobody asks your name, and the exercise book closes on the day without a line in it for you.
outcomes.failure:
The barricade stays visible far longer than distance says it should, so you push the loop wider, then wider again, correcting against a horizon that offers nothing to correct against. Heat gathers under your clothes. The salt takes water out of every breath you spend on it.

You regain the eastern track late with your legs gone stupid and your last meal too far behind to argue with. From the raised road the umbrella is a small striped shape you could have walked past in twenty minutes, and it has not moved all day.

outcomes.outcome: You tell the collectors what the eastern road actually holds: the crater route that killed two of theirs, the quiet water, the places where travelers died for nothing. The clerk writes it all down in her exercise book while the old man listens without blinking. When you finish, he waves you through and keeps your account instead of your rations. Walking on costs nothing, and the road feels briefly like something people share.

events.body: A blue line trembles where the salt meets the sky. It widens when you look away and slides against your own movement instead of with it. At its far end a low dark ridge stands above the crust like a reef, and the ridge is walking. Nothing else out here is that size; colossus is the only word your mouth finds for it. Broken stakes nearby carry cloth strips still damp in air that should have dried them hours ago. The crust ahead is split into long parallel fractures, too straight for wind. Your map shows no water this way.

outcomes.success: You give up the blue line and take the walking ridge's bearing instead, keeping well off its ground. Where it rested through the worst heat, the salt lies dark for forty strides, and water has gathered under corrugated metal at its low center: a rain trap with one bottle still sealed in the catch box. The afternoon is gone. The cap has never been lifted.
outcomes.failure: The blue line keeps exactly one swell of salt between itself and you, hour after hour, and the dark ridge sits farther off at dusk than it did at noon. You stop where your own crossing footprints come back to meet you. Legs finished, nothing eaten since morning, and the water still trembling at the distance it started from.

outcomes.success: You put your back to the horizon and read the ground instead. The fractures run in long parallel sets, too straight for weather, and they lead back to the shape that opened them. You hold the road on the unbroken side. The blue line slides away sideways as you walk, and the afternoon stays yours.
outcomes.failure: Salt and cloud throw the light back with equal force, and the fracture lines run out under glare before you can follow them into a bearing. You choose east, correct it, then correct the correction. The road survives the arithmetic. Your legs pay for every reference you could not trust.

events.body: A fuel tanker rests axle-deep in salt, cab peeled open by heat. The rear cargo locker stays sealed under white mineral crust, warning diamonds faded to ghosts. Petroleum gathers at the hinges. Something heavy shifts inside.

outcomes.success: Your cut follows the weakest seam. The locker opens on road flares, good metal, and a framed pack in oilskin. One flare casing is hand-repacked: a smoke charge.
outcomes.failure: Your edge throws one bright spark into trapped vapor. Flame punches out and rolls over your arms before open air starves it. You retreat burned, the locker warped shut.

outcomes.success: You loosen the lower hinge and wait out the fumes. When the smell thins, you open up: a scrap shotgun and two dry shells under a driver’s coat.
outcomes.failure: The gauge reads clean because heat killed its sensor. Your first breath inside fills your lungs with bitter vapor. You escape coughing, ribs and steps aching.

outcomes.outcome: You walk the fume line slowly, breathing shallow through your sleeve, and come out the far side steady. Your body learns to hold pain aside.

events.body: A brown dust wall climbs from salt to cloud in the north, swallowing wrecks one by one. Static lifts your hair; buckles strike your pack. A chained truck frame offers low shelter. A culvert opens farther east.

outcomes.success: You crawl under the truck frame and wrap its chain across your pack. Dust blacks out daylight and bucks the steel above, but the anchor holds. Salt fills every seam.
outcomes.failure: The chain slips at the first impact. Dust drives through cloth, eyes, and throat while you wrestle the frame. You emerge coughing, lungs full of grit.

outcomes.success: You reach the culvert as the front swallows the last wreck. Momentum carries you down the concrete slope into dark and old water. Dust passes overhead, missing your lungs.
outcomes.failure: The wall catches you strides from the opening. Wind hurls you across open salt, filling every breath with earth. You reach the culvert bruised, winded, and shaken.

events.body: Human bones ring a single fresh boot print, wired so wind cannot move them. Inside, the salt lies darker and smoother, the way the pan closes over brine. Intact boots wait by the skull, toes pointing away.

outcomes.success: The circle marks thin crust over a pit; the lone print is a last backward step. Dark salt is a wake with nothing beneath. You leave by the open side.
outcomes.failure: You read the pattern only as dark crust opens under your weight. One leg sinks into hot slurry before you drag free. Radiation and pain climb together.

outcomes.success: You walk the print’s exact line and lift the boots clear of the circle. Their leather will cut into repairs, and three pistol rounds hide beneath one insole.
outcomes.failure: The salt collapses under your reaching leg. You wrench free before the pit takes your knee, but chemical heat burns upward through the boot. The pair stays put.

events.body:
Three carts come on in single file, plated with road signs cut and overlapped like scales, every plate polished until the line of them throws light you can feel on your face. Narrow slots break the plating at chest height. Nothing shows through them.

The lead cart stops well beyond speaking range. A square mirror rises on a mast from its roof and gives you four deliberate bursts, waits, and gives them again. Above the roof behind it a folding awning frame stands stripped to its ribs, the fabric torn away along its seams, and the two people working under that frame are working in full sun.

The wrecks off the track could hide you. Their metal has been taking sun since dawn and their shadows are already thinner than your body. Whatever these people are, they cross salt that carries no road on any map you own, and they are still alive to signal about it.

outcomes.success:
You give back the old peaceful sequence, slow enough to be read as courtesy rather than as an answer, and you stand with your hands open and well away from your pack while the mirror decides.

A side hatch opens the width of a forearm. The trade is conducted through it: what the road behind you is doing, which wrecks still hold shade, where the crust has gone soft. Two bottles and four cartridges come back out. The masks stay on, mirrored and blank, and the voice behind them is young and careful and says nothing that is not about road.
outcomes.failure:
Your last flash lands a beat wrong and turns a greeting into the convoy's own signal for armed pursuit. You learn this only from what happens next.

The shots go into the salt on either side of you, close enough to throw grit into your teeth, and you go down onto crust that opens both forearms while three carts grind past at walking speed. Nobody fires twice. Nobody stops. The restraint is worse than anger would have been, because it means they read you correctly the second time and did not need to shoot.

outcomes.success:
You get under a delivery chassis before the mirror comes around and pull salt cloth over everything on you that shines. The metal above holds the whole morning's heat against your back.

The carts pass near enough that axle heat crosses your face and you can hear a hand working a signal lamp's shutter, unhurried. None of them slows. The mirrors keep talking to the horizon behind you, four bursts and a wait, four bursts and a wait, until distance takes the light out of them.
outcomes.failure:
The lead cart stops beside your wreck. It does not search. It sits there with its slots facing the salt while the sun climbs, and you learn that waiting is a weapon anybody can afford.

Hot metal presses through your clothes. Minutes become an hour. When they finally roll east you come out with your mouth gummed shut and your hands unsteady, and you do not stop to eat, because sitting down feels like a decision you might not reverse. You will never know whether they knew.

outcomes.success:
You rebuild the awning from mirror stock, salvaged rod, and the torn fabric's own hems, working the whole hour under a firing slot that never quite looks away from your hands.

When it is done the crew run the frame out and back twice, then leave it standing and put two of their own people in the shade under it. The trade arrives without discussion: a layered dust cloak, waxed and heavy, pushed through the hatch by a gloved hand. Nobody thanks you. The shade is the thanks, and they know you can see it.
outcomes.failure:
Your frame takes shape and holds until the first real gust, and then it folds along the joint you were least sure of, slowly, across the cart roof, while the slots watch.

The crew wave you back before you can get under it again. One of them begins stripping your rod out of the folded frame with the flat patience of somebody who has repaired this awning before and expects to repair it again. You leave carrying the hour, the effort, and their politeness, which is the least useful of the three.

outcomes.success:
You trade the only thing you own that they cannot read from a cart: the road behind you. Which wrecks hold shade past noon and which have gone to rust powder. Where the crust turns soft enough to take a wheel to the axle. The stretch where wind has erased the ruts entirely and the ground stops helping anyone.

They set it against their own logs and find two things they did not have. A gloved hand passes back a bone die, rounded, its six almost worn away. What it costs you is that the road behind you is no longer yours alone to know.
outcomes.failure:
They already carry that stretch in their logs, corrected twice by scouts who went and looked. You hear it in the pause before the mirror answers: not contempt, only the small silence of people handed something they filed last season.

The hatch does not open. A voice through the plate thanks you for stopping and suggests the wrecks for shade, which is either courtesy or an instruction. You spend the rest of the hour explaining yourself to sealed steel, and you walk away from it in stages.

events.body: Cracked solar panels turn sunward with slow insect clicks, wave after wave without wind. A controller cabinet still shows green. Reliable shade lies beneath several panels — if you trust machinery already adjusting for afternoon.

outcomes.success: You isolate the controller before opening its cabinet, keeping the grid asleep. Charge parts and a sealed stimulant fit your pack. Behind you one row freezes mid-turn.
outcomes.failure: Stored current crosses your tool and knots every muscle at once. You wake on hot salt, thoughts arriving out of order. The panels keep turning above, indifferent.

outcomes.success: You pick a panel whose belt already split. Its shadow holds still while the others creep. Ten quiet minutes slow your breathing and return strength.
outcomes.failure: The panel wakes mid-rest and turns its black face away. Full sun finds you before sleep becomes recovery. You leave wearier, tracked by clicking rows.

events.body: A new crater interrupts the road, its glass floor clicking as buried heat escapes. Survey flags around the rim are clean enough to have been placed within days, but no crew or vehicle remains. One flag bears a strip of lead shielding tied like mourning cloth. The direct route skirts the lowest edge. A longer arc stays beyond the range where your teeth begin to taste of metal.

outcomes.success: You follow the survey flags rather than the tempting glass. A lead-lined case lies beneath the final marker, holding radiation tablets and a purifier ampoule. Whoever abandoned the rim left treatment where another careful person might find it.
outcomes.failure: The scanner reacts only after warmth has entered your boots and a metallic taste coats your tongue. A buried hot pocket has dosed you through the crust. You retreat along your own prints, carrying radiation no distance can immediately remove.

outcomes.outcome: You keep the lead-marked flags at the edge of vision and walk the crater’s full circumference. The detour consumes daylight, food, and strength, but the clicking glass never passes beneath your feet and the missing survey crew remains unexplained.

events.body: Numbers repeat beneath the receiver’s wind noise: six figures, a pause, then four more spoken by a voice stripped of emotion. The sequence restarts whenever you cross a low ridge. No callsign or emergency phrase accompanies it. Rusted stakes nearby form an incomplete grid in the salt. The broadcast may describe coordinates, a bearing, an inventory, or a system continuing work after every intended listener disappeared.

outcomes.success: You separate grid coordinates from the repeated inventory code. Beneath the correct stake waits a sealed canister containing medicine and three rifle rounds. The transmission stops after you lift it, as though a distant system has checked off delivery.
outcomes.failure: You replay the sequence until each number seems capable of replacing every other. The sun crosses an hour of sky while your notes become less coherent. You leave the stakes unfollowed, concentration shaken by a voice that never noticed your confusion.

outcomes.success: You ignore the sequence’s meaning and measure only where the signal strengthens. Its bearing holds east across three ridges, correcting a road almost erased by wind. The numbers continue, useful without becoming understood.
outcomes.failure: Metal wrecks reflect the signal and make north sound stronger than east. You follow one clear bearing into your earlier tracks. Recognizing the circle saves the day, but not the strength already spent walking it.

events.body:
The fire is small and burning inside the steel rim of an overturned truck wheel, which is how you know it was laid by somebody who intends to leave no mark on the salt. You see it from a long way out. After sunset out here there is nothing else to see.

A woman sits beyond the smoke with both hands open on her knees, which is a thing people do on purpose. One blanket. Two cups, both set out. A covered pot near enough to the coals to be keeping rather than cooking. A second bedroll lies unrolled on the far side of the fire with nobody in it.

She does not search the dark for you. She says, loud enough to carry and no louder, that her name is Noma, that there is water and enough of the pot for two, and that the bedroll has been empty since the flats before this one. Then she stops talking and lets you decide. Spilled water is already hardening into a pale scab beside her boot.

outcomes.success:
You come in and sit where she can see your hands, and she pours without comment.

Her talk is a list, which is how she keeps track: who is walking the north pan and how many, which wells are answering, a man by the tanker wrecks who trades fair and a woman past him who does not, three names she says once and does not explain. You sleep in turns. She takes first watch unasked and wakes you when she said she would.

At dawn she pushes two ration bars into your pack past your objection and walks east beside you for miles before her road bends off yours.
outcomes.failure:
Warmth and four days of walking beat your caution between them. You go down hard and sleep like something switched off.

You wake to a folded blanket, coals banked so they would still be alive for you, two cups scoured with sand and set upside down, and your pack a hand's width from where you left it with the strap rebuckled by somebody who was in no hurry at all. Whatever was in it worth carrying out is not in it now.

Her tracks go east. She left you the fire, which is not what a thief does, and she took what she took anyway.

outcomes.success:
You go downwind and keep wreck iron between yourself and the light, walking on crust that is already broken so nothing new has to break under you.

She does not turn around. She stirs the pot, sets the lid back, and says the thing about the water and the pot once more into the dark, in case the dark had not finished thinking about it. Then she stops offering and eats.

The second bedroll stays where it is, flat and visible, until distance and darkness close over it together. Neither accepted nor withdrawn. You walk east with the road to yourself, which is what you asked for.
outcomes.failure:
Your boot goes through a salt crust with a crack that carries like a shot across flat ground.

Noma is off the bedroll and out of the firelight before the sound has finished. You are down behind a wheel hub with your pulse in your ears, and now there is nothing either of you can do except be two shapes in the dark who have each decided the other might be a problem. She calls out once. You do not answer, because answering would place you.

You leave in a wide arc. Behind you the fire burns between two people who both retreated from it.

events.body:
A trader stops a long stride beyond grabbing distance, lowers the handles of a one-wheeled cart, and sets a stone on the road between you to mark the line neither of you will cross. Tin cups chime under the canvas until the wheel finishes settling.

The stock is modest and real: canned meat, dressings boiled pale, a jar of fasteners sorted by thread. A hand scale hangs from the frame with its lead counterweight already resting in the pan, and they tap it twice so you can watch it swing true before anything of yours goes near it.

The price arrives before you ask for it. One bundle of clean salvage per trade, weighed on that scale, and nothing on credit. What they have seen of the road costs only your patience, since a trader who walks the same three stretches over and over has more of that than they can sell. Then they wait, to learn which of the two you came for.

outcomes.success:
You sort the bundle before it reaches the pan, clean fasteners in one palm and rusted stock in the other, and you let them watch you do it. That changes the weight, and the weight changes the conversation. The counterweight comes off once and goes back on lighter, which is the entire negotiation.

Across the stone comes a tin of meat and a roll of dressings that still smells of the pot it was boiled in. They lift the cart handles, then stand a moment longer than the trade required, working out which way you will turn.
outcomes.failure:
You put the bundle up before you look at what sits under the counterweight, and they let you. There is a second lead disc bolted beneath the first. It is not a cheat, only a weight neither of you named aloud, and naming weights was your half of the work.

The bundle buys one ration bar. They recite each measure while handing it over, the number and then the name for the number, so that nothing here can be called theft afterward. You have paid good fasteners for an afternoon's lesson in the cost of hurry.

outcomes.success:
They do not tell you the road ahead is dangerous, which is what a useless account sounds like. They tell you that the birds along an eastern culvert lift about four breaths before armed travelers come round the bend, every time, and that the birds are the part worth trusting.

You test it against what you already know and it holds. Nothing changes hands. You walk on carrying a rule instead of an object, and for the rest of the day your attention keeps going to the tops of things: wires, gutter lines, wall ridges, anywhere a bird would choose to sit.
outcomes.failure:
The account opens confidently and spends the rest of itself correcting. A grain tower that burned years ago is the first landmark; when you say so, they move it, then move a bridge that is lying in its own river to make room, then put the tower back where it started.

You stay through three versions because the fourth might agree with itself. It does not. You leave with no bearing you would follow after dark, and with the particular tiredness that comes of listening hard to nothing at all.

events.body: The first drop hisses on a road sign and leaves a white-rimmed pit. More strike the pavement in a widening pattern, lifting smoke from metal and dead leaves. Clouds have gathered without thunder, their lower edges stained yellow. Broken panels nearby could become a roof if joined quickly. The eastern road remains open, but exposed buckles already feel warm where the rain touches them.

outcomes.success: You overlap painted panels so each seam drains away from the next. Acid rattles above while clean air survives beneath. When the shower thins, your shelter is scarred into lace, but your skin and essential gear remain protected.
outcomes.failure: The lowest seam runs inward instead of out. Caustic water tracks down your sleeve and pools against your side before you tear free. The shelter collapses behind you, leaving raw skin and the strength spent building it.

outcomes.success: You cover exposed metal and maintain a pace the short cloud cannot match. Drops smoke from your outer layers without reaching skin. Clear air returns behind the shower, though the sprint leaves your breathing rough.
outcomes.failure: The rain lasts beyond the rhythm you chose. It eats through shoulder cloth and follows pack straps toward skin, forcing you onward while every adjustment exposes another place. You outwalk the cloud raw beneath your straps, depleted, and smelling of wet metal.

events.body: A clean canvas backpack sits upright in the center of the road. Its straps have been folded beneath it and its top flap buckled as though displayed in a shop. Dust has collected everywhere except a narrow line running from the pack toward a drainage pipe. No footprints approach it. Someone took time to erase them—or placed the pack without ever stepping onto the road.

outcomes.success: The pale line leads to a wire trigger hidden beneath grit. You pin its spring and cut the charge free before touching the pack. Inside wait canned meat, pistol rounds, and enough sound canvas to carry them properly.
outcomes.failure: A second wire lies beneath the buckle where inspection brings your hand closest. The snap charge drives fragments into your palm and wrist. You retreat empty-handed, blood running across the straps you meant to claim cleanly.

outcomes.outcome: You give the display a wide edge and never turn your back to the drainage pipe. The pack remains upright behind you, complete with whatever supplies or violence made it so carefully visible. Nothing follows before the next bend.

The wire lifts on your second fingertip without a click. Pistol rounds roll out of the side pocket into your palm, brass warm from the sun. The work leaves your hands awake and quick for whatever the road asks next.

events.body: A stranger sits against a kilometer stone with both hands pressed around a wound beneath the ribs. Their coat has been cut open rather than torn, and a trail of dark cloth markers leads back along the road. A stamped route token hangs from their neck. They keep glancing toward the markers, listening for companions, attackers, or the person they expect to return and finish the work. Your own coat is lined with cloth that would fold into a pad, though holding a wound closed by hand is slow work with no clean end.

outcomes.success: You clean the wound, pack it, and bind the stranger tightly enough to slow the bleeding. Before standing, they give you the stamped token used by road traders. Relief steadies both their pulse and your conviction that effort still matters.
outcomes.failure: The wound reaches deeper than cloth and pressure can repair. You remain while the stranger’s grip weakens, learning the name attached to the route token but not taking it. Their final minutes contain another voice instead of the empty road.

outcomes.outcome: You hold the bottle while the stranger drinks, then stop before generosity becomes treatment you cannot provide. They point out a trail hidden behind the marker stone. It shortens your route; it does not answer what happens after you leave.

outcomes.success: You cut the lining from your own coat, fold it into a pad, and lean on the wound with your whole weight. The bleeding slows. By the time the people behind the markers answer your shouting, the stranger is awake enough to argue with them, and your arms will not stop shaking.
outcomes.failure: You press until your hands go numb, but the wound fills faster than cloth can hold it. The stranger stops trying to speak partway through. When the markers finally bring someone back along the road, you are still kneeling there with a ruined coat and nothing to hand over.

events.body: A weatherproof route map stands beneath cracked glass, its printed roads buried under layers of scratched amendments. Arrows contradict one another. Names have been crossed out, restored, and crossed out again in different hands. A strip of red cloth marks one eastern route; three separate warnings call it safe, flooded, and occupied. There is room near the bottom for one more traveler to add certainty or confusion.

outcomes.success: You compare ink age, flood lines, and the direction from which each warning was scratched. A consistent route emerges beneath the argument. Understanding the layers returns time and focus the road normally consumes.
outcomes.failure: Every correction depends on another mark whose date cannot be trusted. You follow the debate around the glass until its contradictions cost more time than choosing blindly. The map remains crowded with confidence and poor evidence.

outcomes.success: You scratch a precise warning beside a collapsed culvert, including the landmark that reveals it before danger. The note occupies little space but restores a sense that knowledge can move east even when people do not.
outcomes.failure: Your tool skates over old cuts and reduces the warning to another pale line among hundreds. From two steps away, it cannot be distinguished from vandalism. You leave no clearer guidance than you found.

events.body: The road offers a mile without smoke, voices, tracks, or movement in the weeds. Even the wind has lowered enough that your gear no longer answers every step. An intact drainage grate lies beside a shallow ditch, but nothing suggests anyone has disturbed it recently. The absence of danger feels almost staged. You can accept the quiet as shelter or spend it searching for the reason nothing else stopped here.

outcomes.outcome: You loosen your pace and let your shoulders fall from the position they use around threats. No ambush interrupts the mile. By its end, fatigue has receded enough that the empty road feels like a gift rather than unfinished evidence.

outcomes.success: The grate lifts without revealing wire, prints, or occupied darkness. Two useful metal assemblies sit above the dry channel, washed clean by older rain. You pack them and leave the unexplained quiet mostly intact.
outcomes.failure: You inspect the ditch, the grate, and every patch of flattened weed until calm has become labor. Nothing reveals itself. The mile ends with less energy and no better explanation for why it was safe.

events.body: A roadside cairn bears a name, two dates, and the words THEY KEPT WALKING. Each stone comes from a different kind of ground: red factory brick, black marsh slate, pale salt, and a piece of fused glass. A narrow gap beneath the inscription could shelter a message or emergency ration. Whoever built the marker expected other travelers to stop long enough to decide what respect requires.

outcomes.outcome: You add a stone from the road behind you, changing the cairn’s balance by almost nothing. The inscription no longer belongs only to the buried person. For several miles, its stubborn plural gives purpose to your own continued movement.

outcomes.success: Beneath the outer stones lies a ration wrapped in waxed cloth and marked FOR THE NEXT ONE. You take it without disturbing the central grave, accepting a provision deliberately left for hunger rather than remembrance.
outcomes.failure: Your search reaches packed earth and the edge of burial cloth. There is no cache, only a body arranged with care. You replace every stone, but the cairn’s words follow as accusation rather than encouragement.

events.body: A white parachute hangs from power lines over a pod nosed into the roadside, fabric still moving. A lit keypad glows beside a scoured code panel; the shell ticks at something unexplained. Nothing has weathered. Open it here, or drag it under the awning unseen.

outcomes.success: You enter the faded code before the pod repeats its signal. The latch gives medicine, tablets, one ration. A fast-draw holster rides the straps. You clear out fast.
outcomes.failure: The third wrong entry wakes a recovery alarm that crosses the ruins. You abandon the sealed pod and run, every echo suggesting footsteps or machines already turning.

outcomes.success: You haul the pod behind concrete on its parachute lines and open it unseen. Two bottles and canned meat wait inside; the cut line coils into ten meters of rope.
outcomes.failure: The buried nose won’t budge till your leg braces wrong. Something tears under the effort. The casing sits ticking and visible while your joint slows the leaving.

events.body: A courier bicycle leans against a route marker, chain snapped, rear wheel lifted clear of the ground. The rider is gone and took the sidearm with them: the holster stitched to the crossbar is empty, its flap still buttoned back. What they did not take is the locked cargo box, and someone since has scratched the keyway raw trying it without a key. A faded manifest names medical deliveries along roads that no longer connect. Wire and enough patience to lace it through might make the chain turn again.

outcomes.success: You lace the broken links with wire and keep your weight forward. The bicycle carries you over several clean kilometers before the repair unwinds. You leave it beneath another marker with distance gained and strength restored.
outcomes.failure: Wire goes into the chain and will not hold two turns together. You splice it three times; the third splice takes a strip of skin off your knuckle before it parts like the others did. Whatever you fed into the repair comes back out twisted past use. You leave the bicycle against the marker exactly as you found it.

outcomes.success: You set the pry beside the keyway rather than in it and let the lid's own hinge give first. The medical run the manifest promises went out long ago; what remains under the paperwork is the ration the courier was saving and a strip of cartridges for the sidearm they walked away with. You take both.
outcomes.failure: Your pick snaps below the pins and the broken half seats itself where a key should go. Whatever you shaped it from is inside the lock now and will not come out. The box holds against you and against everyone after you, short of a drill and an hour nobody on this road has.

events.body: Hairless crows line a guardrail in order of size, their exposed throats pulsing before each borrowed sound: half a name, a request for water, laughter that stops too sharply. One says TURN LEFT in three different voices. Another wears bandage cloth wound twice around its leg. Below the rail, where they drop what they cannot eat, wire and small fittings have gathered into a seam of shine along the concrete. The flock watches to see whether stolen language moves you the way hunger moves them.

outcomes.success: You follow the repeated phrase only after identifying which bird learned it most recently. The words lead to an abandoned camp where canned meat and clean bandages remain under canvas. The flock waits overhead for whatever you expose.
outcomes.failure: The voices take you down into a basin where lichen glows under the stones and the air tastes of hot coins. By the time you understand what the glow is telling you, you are standing in the middle of it and the flock has lifted beyond reach, laughing in a stranger's laugh.

outcomes.victory: They come in ragged waves until enough of them strike the road that the rest reconsider and lift away, still talking in other people's voices. What they had been guarding is wedged under the rail: bandage cloth, wire, fittings, sorted by nothing except shine. You take the cloth and the metal and leave the rest of the hoard where it lies.

events.body: Clouds split without warning and reveal a sky whose blue seems invented. Sunlight restores color to rust, weeds, and old paint for several minutes. Far landmarks sharpen enough to compare against the map, but distant movement also becomes visible on two separate ridges. The open sky offers rest from dimness or information about what lies ahead, never enough time to take both completely.

outcomes.outcome: You stop where sunlight reaches the road and breathe without searching every shadow. Warmth eases tension from your back. By the time clouds close again, any fear you were still carrying has loosened enough to move normally.

outcomes.success: You compare both ridges, the road’s bend, and a distant column of smoke before haze returns. One route avoids the movement entirely. The brief survey organizes the next hours into choices rather than surprises.
outcomes.failure: A glint on the northern ridge keeps changing shape, holding your attention after every useful landmark has been recorded. When clouds return, you have spent the clear interval watching something that may never have moved.

events.body: Sunlight catches a wire stretched just above ankle height. It crosses the trail between a bent sapling and a drainage post, too clean to be old debris. The obvious trigger is visible once noticed; a second line may be hidden where cautious travelers step around the first. No voices answer the wind. Whoever set the snare may be gone, watching, or relying on the road to do their waiting.

outcomes.success: You pin the sapling before cutting tension from the trigger. The wire, spring, and fastening hooks come away intact enough to reuse. No observer interferes while their patient mechanism becomes weight in your own pack.
outcomes.failure: The trigger includes a slack loop disguised beneath leaves. It tightens when you reach for the visible wire and whips your legs sideways. You strike the road hard, ankle twisting while the empty trail offers no witness to the trap’s success.

outcomes.success: You mark both anchor points and step beyond their likely reach. Nothing tightens around boot or pack. The wire remains armed behind you, preserving your safety at the possible expense of the next less observant traveler.
outcomes.failure: A second line waits exactly where the first one taught you to step, and it takes the pack instead of the ankle. The side pocket opens along its seam while you are still turning. Whatever it was carrying goes into the dust, and you spend a while cutting free of a wire meant for something smaller than you.

events.body: Wind has erased the marked road until every shallow depression resembles a route east. Ruined shapes emerge through dust, lose their edges, and return in different positions. No signal reaches the receiver and no recent track survives long enough to follow. A line of old marker posts offers steady direction; the debris gathered around them may conceal supplies, holes, or nothing worth the strength required to search.

outcomes.success: You count marker posts and hold the same bearing whenever dust hides the next one. The rhythm survives the empty stretch without stealing unnecessary strength. Eventually, a recognizable road cut appears exactly where the old line promised.
outcomes.failure: Two posts have fallen and turn the steady line into a slow correction across loose ground. You recover the route before becoming lost, but the featureless distance consumes more energy than its map measurement deserved.

outcomes.success: Beneath a marker tilted away from the wind, you find a ration sealed inside a survey tube. Its paper label has faded, but the wrapper remains unbroken. The road offers one useful answer after all.
outcomes.failure: You open broken cases, lift sheets of metal, and inspect hollows already emptied by animals. Dust restores each disturbed place behind you. The search produces no supplies and turns an uneventful mile into avoidable exhaustion.
